correctness.rationale: The equivariant Quillen map is explicitly described and verified on the H-fixed lower fibers. For every H-stable flat, fixed nerve simplices are orbit unions, and nonempty invariant convex intersections admit fixed witnesses by averaging. Orbit-intersection convex sets cover V^H, using an antipodal pair in the flat; the nerve is contractible. DAGs similarly form a genuine equivariant nerve of the augmentation sphere. Transitive H kills the augmentation-sphere fixed part, and regular invariant partitions are subgroup cosets. Explicit complete small finite tests agree with predicted fixed topology and Lie character; finite checks are corroborative only. The case n=2 is excluded to avoid an empty-factor join boundary.

originality.rationale: The 1999 and 2004 directed-graph results assert ordinary sphere-wedge types; the closely inspected 2023 constellation paper proves the nonequivariant join by ordinary lower fibers. The new mathematical statement is a genuine equivariant equivalence, established by proving contractibility of every H-fixed fiber through convex orbit intersections. It has the concrete consequence that every finite-group proper subgroup lattice is realized as a geometric fixed space. No inspected statement implies this without a new fixed-fiber argument. Earlier full texts inaccessible in part, so the novelty assessment remains conditional on that residual risk.
residual_risks: The complete 1999 Björner–Welker article and complete 2004 Hultman article were not inspected; an equivalent equivariant result hidden in them is not ruled out.
The 2023 proof supplies the same underlying poset map and convex cover; the extension may be implicit to specialists, and priority should be independently assessed.
Database indexing cannot establish novelty or exclusivity.

value.rationale: This supplies a uniform structural answer to every subgroup-fixed homotopy question for a classical infinite symmetric digraph-complex family and realizes arbitrary finite-group subgroup-lattice order complexes in a natural geometric fixed space. The cyclic arithmetic trichotomy and elementary abelian building wedges illustrate substantive new topological behavior beyond ordinary sphere counts; it is not a selected unmotivated finite slice.
